title: Binance Works to Recover Billions After Major Hack
summary: On October 30, 2026, the cryptocurrency company Binance said it was working to recover digital assets worth billions of dollars after a major hack. The company said about $3 billion of the stolen assets had been secured, but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. The total amount involved was reported as more than $6.3 billion. Binance is a large exchange where people trade digital assets, and it is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. At first, the company thought the breach may have started with one engineer's laptop. Later, it said its investigation had found additional points of breach, and that the attack was wider than first thought. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the attack was not carried out by one person. He also said the hackers used a tool that destroyed traces as they went, making the investigation harder to follow. In the United States, the Secret Service said it was working to identify, freeze, trace, and recover the stolen funds, and Binance said it was also working with the FBI. Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, but investigators could still help track the funds, an effort that generally involves law enforcement in different countries. Binance told users their money was safe and that it was covering every loss. It said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets. It had first paused deposits and withdrawals, then said deposits remained unaffected. Some experts warned that customers should check what they had been promised in their contracts, because a promise to cover losses may not always be legally binding. For now, Binance says it is strong enough to handle the loss, and the recovery effort continues.
why_it_matters: A hack involving billions of dollars can shake trust in large digital asset exchanges used by millions of people. The recovery effort also matters because tracing stolen funds across countries is difficult, especially when hackers destroy traces as they go.

background_read: A cryptocurrency exchange is a platform where people buy, sell, and trade digital assets, which are forms of money that exist only online and are kept in digital accounts.

Exchanges hold large amounts of customers' digital assets, so they use security systems to protect accounts and track transfers, and they can pause deposits and withdrawals when they suspect a breach.

When digital assets are stolen, recovery is difficult because transfers can move quickly across borders, so exchanges often work with law enforcement agencies in different countries to identify, freeze, and trace the funds.
Customers trust an exchange to keep their money safe, so a large theft raises questions about how the company protects accounts and whether it can cover the losses.
